title: console-cost-trace-atomicity-reduction-and-deferment-plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: cost breakdown and trace views are large surface areas that risk delaying the Console MVP. This ticket captures a surgical reduction strategy that preserves high-value signals while deferring/opt-ing out lower-value atomic tiles. Goal: deliver a minimal, reliable cost + trace experience for launch that keeps SLOs and reduces backend ingestion/compute by ~60% compared to full plan. Scope: - Keep: route-level 7-day cost summary, per-model and per-region top-level breakdown, single-span waterfall for high-impact errors. - Cut or defer: per-token heatmaps, live per-request flamegraphs, heavyweight per-customer breakdown, long-tail attribution tiles. - Add graceful fallbacks: when sampling budget exceeded, UI shows aggregated bucket with CTA to opt-in for detailed view. - Operational guardrails: trace sampling thresholds, deferred-sampling job, telemetry opt-in flag, and a rollback path that re-enables full surface only after load stabilizes.
acceptance_criteria: Route-level 7-day cost summary card is implemented and matches backend billing playground dashboard within 5% for test dataset.
Top-level per-model and per-region aggregated cards render under 300ms on median (CI measurement in staging).
Trace surface shows single-span waterfall for >95% of sampled errors; detailed flamegraph tile replaced by collapsed summary when sampling disabled.
Deferment UX appears when sampling budget exhausted: aggregated bucket plus clear opt-in CTA that opens a short-lived request for elevated sampling.
Backend exposes sampling and aggregation metrics to Console observability with dashboard link and alerts for >10% failure to produce aggregated response.
Rollout plan documented and runbook created with steps to revert to full surface; runbook reviewed and approved by SRE and Product.
MVP launch checklist entry added and signed off by PM, Design, Eng, and SRE for the trimmed surface.
Performance budget validation added to CI; any regression >10% in median render time blocks merge to release branch.
